paragraphs: Meachar detzida asura beshabbat vehi meab melakot, lepikak im hipricha haop ad shehikniso labbayit shechallonotayv setumim o lebebar meqoreh vesatum mikkol tzad venaal bepaneha, o sheradap achar chayya ad shehiknisah labbayit o lechatzer vekayyotze venaal bepaneha, chayyab min hattora; umihu, eno chayyab min hattora ella beheka deen habbayit gadol kol kak, vahare hu yakol litpos hachayya o haop benaqel bimrutza achat, veeno tzarik lebaqqesh tachbulot kede letapeso; abal em habbayit gadol kol kak sheeno yakol lehaggia velitpos haop bimrutza achat mippene shennishmatin mimmennu, vetzarik larutz acharehem betok habbayit ritza shenit o shelishit, hare ellu mechussarim tzeda upatur min hattora, abal midderabbanan asur bekol gavna.

clarification.explanation: Trapping is Torah-forbidden on the Sabbath (one of the primary categories of labor). One who drives a bird into a fully enclosed house, or chases an animal until it enters an enclosed place and locks the door on it, is Torah-liable, provided the place is small enough that he can catch it in a single dash without stratagems. If the place is too large (the animal evades him and he must chase it several times), he is exempt from Torah liability, but it is rabbinically forbidden.
takeaways: Trapping on the Sabbath is forbidden; one is Torah-liable only when catching it is easy (a single dash); in a large place (difficult to catch) one is exempt but it remains rabbinically forbidden

paragraphs: Hatztzad dabar sheeno mechussar tzeda, kegon tzad tzebi chigger o choleh mechamat ayeput, shehu yagea veeno yakol lazuz mimmeqomo, patur min hattora, abal asur midderabbanan; ak hatztzad tzebi yashan o suma o choleh mechamat chom shennolad begupo, chayyab, mippene shehem asuyim lehishshamet keshemmargishim yede-adam, umechussere tzeda hem.

clarification.explanation: An animal that is "actually incapable of being caught" is not considered trapped (like a lame or sick deer that cannot move) — one is exempt from Torah liability, but it is rabbinically forbidden. An animal that could escape the moment it senses a person's presence (even if asleep, blind, or feverish) — one is liable, since it is considered "apt to escape."
takeaways: An animal entirely unable to flee (disabled, utterly exhausted) — exempt; one that could escape if it woke up or was discovered — liable

paragraphs: Tzebi veop shenniknas lecheder vekayyotze, venaal bepanayv, chayyab; veim naalu shenayim, peturin min hattora vechayyabim midderabbanan. veim lo haya yakol echad lenaalu venaalu shenayim, chayyabin min hattora. veim hayu hatztzebi o haop bacheder vehaya haddelet sagur, muttar lekattechilla linol bemanul, demeachar shehaddelet sagur en yakol libroach, vahare hem shemurim veomedim, ubemanul hu mosip shemira, veen bazeh mishshum tzeda.

clarification.explanation: An animal that entered a room and had the door locked on it — one is liable; if two people locked it together, they are exempt from Torah liability (though rabbinically liable), unless one of them could not have done it alone and only the two together succeeded — in which case they are Torah-liable. And if the door was already closed (the animal could no longer escape), it is permitted as the primary practice to lock it with a bolt as well, since this is merely an additional safeguard and not new trapping.
takeaways: Locking a door that was already closed (a mere additional safeguard) is permitted, since it does not constitute new trapping

paragraphs: Mi shehaya lo tzebi qashur bebeto, muttar linol haddelet bepanayv kede lehosip shemira al shemirato, ki meachar shehaya hatztzebi qashur - nitztzod veomed hu. veim achar shennaal haddelet nittar hatztzebi miqqeshirato, denimtza atta nitztzod veshamur mikkoach haddelet, en mechayyebim oto liptoach haddelet kede lebattel shemirato, mippene shebbeshaa shennaal, behetter naal, veen atta oseh kelum. veken mi shennaal beto leshamero vehaya op o tzebi betoko, vehu lo haya yodea kelal sheyyesh sham op o tzebi, veachar shennaal noda lo - en mechayyebin oto liptoach haddelet, ella yishshaer naul ad chasheka, kede sheyyabo veyittol hatztzebi o haop mishsham; vehattaam - mippene shekkaasher naal, behetter naal, shello haya yodea sheyyesh tzebi o op; abal im haya yodea sheyyesh tzebi veop uba lisgor haddelet, asur, "p sheen mitkavven latzud otam, ella kavvanato lishmor beto - meachar ki bevadday nitztzod.

clarification.explanation: A deer tied up in the house — it is permitted to lock the door (an additional safeguard on what is already trapped). If, after locking, the deer slips its tie (and is now trapped only by virtue of the door), there is no obligation to open the door, since at the time of locking he acted permissibly. Likewise, one who locked his house for safekeeping and did not know there was a bird or deer inside has no obligation to open it; but if he knew in advance that an animal was there, he is forbidden to lock it, even though his intention is only to safeguard the house (since in effect this is trapping).
takeaways: A locking done permissibly (without knowledge of an animal inside, or when it was already tied) does not obligate opening the door even if the situation later changes

paragraphs: Hechatul, dinah kishar chayya veasur latzud otah. veim niknesa lacheder, asur lisgor happetach ad sheyyotzienna mishsham im yodea shehi sham, "g deeno mitkavven letzudah, vegam eno rotzeh betzayyadtah sheen lo tzorek bazeh kelal, im kol zeh asur im hu yodea shehi sham. al-ken poh irenu bagdad dishkichi chatulim harbeh babbattim, tzerikin lehizzaher bedabar zeh meod - deim niknas lecheder ulekol maqom sheyyesh lo petach lenaalo veroeh sheyyesh sham chatul, lo yinal happetach ella ad sheyyotzi hechatul mishsham.

clarification.explanation: A cat has the law of a wild animal — it is forbidden to trap it. If it entered a room and it is known to be there, it is forbidden to close the door (even without intent or desire to trap it) until it is removed. In Baghdad, where cats are common in houses, one must be very careful: before locking any door, one should check whether a cat is inside.
takeaways: A cat that entered a room — the door may not be locked until it leaves, even without intent to trap it

paragraphs: Zebubin asur letzudam midderabbanan; velaken tzarik lehizzaher shello lisgor teba o listom keli sheyyesh sham zebubin, mippene shehem nitztzodin bisgira zo; v"p sheeno mitkavven letzudam, mikkol maqom "pesiq resheh velo yamut" hu. ketzad yaaseh? yapricha hazzebubin techilla vech"k yekasseh hakkeli o yisgor hatteba. bammeh debarim amurim? kesheroeh zebubin beenayv, abal im eno roeh, eno mechuyyab libdoq im yesh sham zebubin. veken im raa vehiprichan, eno mechuyyab libdoq im nishar ezeh zebub sham, dekevan shehu sapeq - soger kedarko veeno choshesh, deen kan "pesiq resheh". veasur lehaamid sam-hammavet lazzebubin beshabbat.

clarification.explanation: Flies are rabbinically forbidden to trap; therefore one should not close a box or vessel with flies inside (this is trapping, an inevitable result). One should first chase them out and only then close it. This applies specifically when one actually sees flies; there is no obligation to check when none are seen, and even if one chased them out and is not certain none remained, there is no concern (a mere doubt). It is forbidden to set out poison for flies on the Sabbath.
takeaways: Before closing a vessel or box, visible flies should first be chased out; a doubt as to whether any remained is not a concern

paragraphs: Asur lehaamid beshabbat hammetzuda latzud bah akbarim, veal-ken hammetzuda chashib keli shemmelakto leissur veasur letaltelah mishshum muqtzeh. vehinneh lipamim maamidim hammetzuda meereb-shabbat, venitztzod bah haakbar ballayla, tzerikin lizzaher shello yasiru mimmenna haakbar beyom shabbat mishshum muqtzeh, ella yishshaer bah ad motzae-shabbat.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to set a mousetrap on the Sabbath, and it is therefore "a utensil whose function is for a forbidden purpose" (muktzeh). If it was set before the Sabbath and a mouse was caught during the night, it may not be removed on the Sabbath day (muktzeh), but one should wait until the conclusion of the Sabbath.
takeaways: A mousetrap is muktzeh; a mouse caught before the Sabbath remains in the trap until the Sabbath's conclusion

paragraphs: Avazim vetarnegolim vekayyotze haggedelim birshuto shel adam, asur letzudam, dehaynu lehaknisam tok hallul shellahem o letok cheder acher velisgor happetach alehem kede shello yetzeu; la mibbaaya im maredu veyatzeu min hallul deasur min hattora lehaknisam letoko, ella apillu im yatzeu min hallul letummam, asur lehachaziram lelul midderabbanan, mippene deellu darkan lihyot moredim chutz likluban, sheyyesh torach letapesam mippene shennishmatin aneh vaana, velaken asur midderabbanan letzudan lehaknisam lallul velisgor alehem; v"p deellu darkam labo leet ereb mealehen lelul, gam ken asur, meachar dehem darkam lihyot moredim chutz likluban sheyyesh torach letapesan; mihu, im en darkan limrod chutz likluban veen torach letapesam, muttar lehaknisam lelul o lecheder echad veyisgor alehem happetach, veayyen bapposeqim. vehinneh hattarnegolim haggedelim poh irenu y", darkam limrod chutz likluban veyesh torach gadol letapesam, velaken tzarik lehazhir hamon haam bazeh - deim yatzeu chutz lallul asur lirdop acharehem ad sheyyaknisem letok hallul o letok cheder veyisgor haddelet; mihu, im yatzeu chutz lechatzer, sheim lo yirdepu acharehem yobdu, hittiru mishshum peseda lirdop acharehem kede lehaknisam letok hechatzer o lebayit gadol sheeno yakol letapesam bo bimrutza achat, ubilbad shello yetaltelem; veayyen acharonim za"l.

clarification.explanation: Geese and chickens under a person's ownership — it is forbidden to trap them (returning them to the coop and closing it on them) if they tend to rebel and flee (making capture difficult). If they do not tend to rebel and there is no difficulty, it is permitted to return them and close the coop. In Baghdad, where the chickens tend to rebel, one must be careful: not to chase them in order to return them to the coop; but if they went out into a public domain and might get lost, it is permitted to chase them to bring them back to the yard (to prevent loss), provided one does not carry them by hand.
takeaways: Rebellious, fleeing poultry (as in Baghdad) may not be forced back into the coop; chasing them to prevent loss (having escaped into a public domain) is permitted, without carrying them by hand

paragraphs: "p shekkatabnu leel deim haya hatztzebi tok hacheder asur linol haddelet, vaapillu im eno mitkavven latzud ella lishmor beto, mikkol maqom avazim vetarnegolim haggedelim bechatzer birshuto, muttar liptoach velinol happetach shel hechatzer veeno choshesh, yaan ki avazim vetarnegolim en bahem tzeda kol kak kemo chayya veop; velaken meachar sheeno mitkavven latzud otam ella noel happetach kedarko lishmor beto, muttar; ak shear chayya vaop deit behu tzeda mammash, sheomedim tok hacheder o tok hechatzer veenam qeshurim o segurim tok keloben, asur linol petach hacheder o hechatzer kedarko v"p sheeno mitkavven letzudam, dinilat haddelet hi shemira lahem vezo hi tzidatam vekannizkar baacharonim za"l. velaken tzarik lehazhir et haam shello yannichu tzebi vekayyotze tok hechatzer bilti qeshira o segira tok hakkelub, deaz asur linol petach hechatzer beshabbat. upoh irenu bagdad yesh harbeh bene-adam sheddarkam legaddel tzebaim bebetam, ak darkam legaddelam sheyyihyu melummadim laamod lemala al haggag o beaksadra tamid velo yeredu lechatzer, ki chosheshim pen yetzeu lirshut-harabbim veyibrechu lachutz, ki en darkam leqasheram. venireh meachar dehatztzebi melummad laamod tamid al haggag o al aksadra, yukal haadam liptoach velinol petach hechatzer happatucha lirshut-harabbim, veraq im nizdammen shehatztzebi yarad lechatzer, az asur linol petach hechatzer. vekol zeh ani koteb leqayyem hamminhag shennahagu bekak, abal yere shamayim yizzaher liqshor et hatztzebi beshabbat velo yismok al hetter zeh, "p shehatztzebi melummad laamod al haggag o al aksadra; vehammitracheq meellu shello legaddelam betok beto legamre, tabo alayv beraka.

clarification.explanation: Even though for a wild animal or bird it is forbidden to lock a door even without intent to trap (since this constitutes actual trapping), for geese and chickens under a person's ownership it is permitted to lock and open the yard door as usual, since there is no real "trapping" of them as there is with a wild animal. But another (genuinely wild) animal or bird that is not tied up or enclosed — it is forbidden to lock the door of the room or yard on the Sabbath, since this is actual trapping of them. In Baghdad they raise deer accustomed to staying on the roof — it is permitted to lock the yard gate (the deer will not come down to it), but if it came down into the yard, it is forbidden; and it is good that one who fears Heaven tie up the deer rather than rely on this leniency, and one who avoids raising such animals altogether — blessing will come upon him.
takeaways: Geese/chickens under ownership (not real trapping) — the yard may be locked as usual; genuinely wild, untied animals or birds — forbidden
A deer accustomed to the roof — the yard may be locked as long as it has not come down; one who fears Heaven should tie it up regardless

paragraphs: Parosh, sheqqorin bearbe "brg'vt", asur letzudo ella im ken hu al besaro veoqetzo; vekol deepshar lehappilo laaretz beli netila beyadayv, yesh laasot ken. veasur laharog parosh, vegam lo yimlelu beyado, gezera shemma yahargennu, ella yittelennu beyado veyizreqennu.

clarification.explanation: A flea — it is forbidden to trap it except when it is on the body and biting, and it is preferable to knock it to the ground rather than pick it up by hand. It is forbidden to kill it, and even to crush it by hand (a decree lest one kill it), but rather one should pick it up and throw it away.
takeaways: A flea touching the body may be removed (preferably by knocking it off, not picking it up), but it may not be killed or crushed

paragraphs: Asur laharog tzira uzebubin veyattushin. vekol hahoreg parosh kehoreg gamal! veyizzaharu haam bedabar zeh lasim alayv en hashgachatam, ubiprat beyattushim hammetzuyim bimot haqqayitz betok hammartep, ki rabbim hemma, vekevan dikeb laadam tuba mechamat aqitzato, az yechereh appo veyakkennu bekappo – sheellu, behannachat hayyad alehem, kerega umlelu vedamam shotet; umeachar sheragil behaki bime hachol, tzarik lasim hashgachato meod beshabbat shello yishkach veyaharog happarosh o hayyattush.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to kill a wasp, flies, or mosquitoes (one who kills a flea is considered, in terms of the severity of the labor, as one who kills a camel). One must be especially careful in summer regarding cellar mosquitoes — not to strike them with the palm out of anger at their bite. Since one is used to doing this during the week, one must watch himself very carefully on the Sabbath not to forget and kill a flea or mosquito.
takeaways: It is forbidden to kill a wasp, flies, and mosquitoes; one must be careful of the habit of swatting mosquitoes in summer

paragraphs: Hammotzi dam meebere hachay, chayyab. vaapillu im lo yatza haddam lachutz mammash, ella shechabal beechad meebere hachay ad shennitzrar haddam tachat haor, shezzeh haddam haya yotze lachutz veraq haor meakkebo, lepikak chayyab mishshum netilat dam, dahare hu keillu yatza lachutz. bammeh debarim amurim? bechobel beadam o bibhema vechayya o beopot o bishmona sheratzim haamurim beparashat shemini, shehem hacholed vehaakbar veku', deillu yesh lahem or; abal hachobel bishar sheqatzim uremasim, kevan deen lahem or, eno chayyab ella ad sheyyetze haddam lachutz. vetzarik lehazhir hamon haam bazeh, ki yesh tippeshim makkim zeh et zeh ad sheyyetze mehem dam lachutz, o yihyeh nitzrar haddam tachat haor; veken yesh harbeh nikshalim bedabar zeh, d"p deeno makkeh et chabero, ella raq topes besar chabero berashe etzbeotayv bekol kocho bechozeq kede letzaaro, veqorin lazeh bearbe "qurtza" (tzebita), ubazeh nitzrar haddam tachat haor; uledaat haramba"m za"l, hachobel beadam o bibhema derek neqama, hare zeh chayyab min hattora, vela have lazeh din melaka sheenah tzerika legupah mishshum deeno tzarik laddam, v"p shehaoseh zot derek sechoq ubedichot dahava lah melaka sheenah tzerika legupah, ha al kol panim chayyab middibre soperim.

clarification.explanation: One who draws blood from the limbs of a living creature is liable, even if the blood did not fully emerge but only became pooled beneath the skin (with only the skin holding it back). This applies to a person, a domesticated animal, a wild animal, a bird, and the eight skinned creeping creatures; for creeping creatures without skin, one is liable only if the blood actually emerges outward. One must be careful: even "pinching" (forcefully pressing fingers together) that causes blood to pool beneath the skin is forbidden. According to the Rambam, one who wounds out of vengeance is Torah-liable (this is not "labor not needed for its own sake"), and one who does so in jest is liable at least rabbinically.
takeaways: Drawing blood (even just pooling it beneath the skin, as with pinching) is forbidden, and one is even Torah-liable for it in creatures with skin

paragraphs: Hakkinna enah mittehuyat min heapar ella min hazzea, lekak muttar leharegah beshabbat. bammeh debarim amurim? bemotze kinna al besaro o shemmatzea al begadayv derek miqreh, abal hampalleh et begadayv mekinim, asur leharegan, ella molelan beyadayv vezoreqan; vehattaam, degazeru shemma yimmatze gam parosh veyabo leharego, kevan dishkichi paroshin bibgadim; lepikak, hampalleh rosho, muttar laharog hakkinnim sheyyimmatze sham, mishshum deen paroshin metzuyim berosh; veim ballayla aqatzo bibsaro veeno yodea im hu kinna o parosh, hare zeh yizreqennu deshemma parosh hu.

clarification.explanation: A louse, according to the Sages, is not generated from a male and female of its kind but from sweat, and therefore it is permitted to kill it on the Sabbath — but only when found by chance on the body or clothing. One who deliberately checks (delouses) clothes for lice may not kill them (a decree lest one also find a flea and kill it), but should crush and discard it. One who checks his own head may kill lice (there are no fleas on the head). One who is bitten at night and does not know whether it is a louse or a flea should discard it without killing, out of doubt.
takeaways: A louse found by chance may be killed; when deliberately checking clothes, one should only crush and discard (out of concern for fleas)

paragraphs: Tob lizzaher millachatzotz shinnayv bemachat, deyesh chashash sheyyotzi dam; veken im mechakkek besaro beshabbat, yizzaher lechakkek benachat velo bechozeq, delipamim nisrak haor veyotze dam veeno margish; veayyen "kap-hachayyim".

clarification.explanation: It is good to be careful not to pick between the teeth with a needle (out of concern for drawing blood), and likewise to be careful, when scratching the skin, not to do so forcefully, lest the skin tear and blood emerge unnoticed.
takeaways: One should avoid picking teeth with a needle, and scratch skin gently, to prevent unintentionally drawing blood

paragraphs: Nachash veaqrab bemaqom sheen memitin - im ratzin acharayv muttar leharegan, veim lav asur ella doreso kedarko keillu eno mekavven leharego, kede sheyyihyeh qetzat shinnuy.

clarification.explanation: A snake or scorpion in a place where they are not deadly (not dangerous) may be killed only if it is chasing after a person; if not, it may not be killed directly, but only trodden upon in the normal course of walking (without direct intent), as a lesser variation.
takeaways: A non-dangerous, non-aggressive snake or scorpion is not killed directly, but may be trodden upon incidentally

paragraphs: Lo yidros bemaqom sheyyesh remasim harbeh kemo nemalim vekayyotze, "p deeno mitkavven leharegam – hava lah paseq resheh vela yamut, shebbevadday yahargem bidrisa. ubime haqqayitz matzuy beirenu nemalim harbeh, veniknasim tok keli shel mayim sheqqorin "abbereq", hammunnach tamid bebet-hakkisse bishbil qinnucha, vehaadam kesheshshopek mayim mizzeh hakkeli al yado kede lirchotz, yoredim nemalim harbeh im hammayim, venimtza hu memit otam beyadayim beet sherochetz, sheyyitmaaku beqinnucha veshipshup, velaken yasimu leb al zot lirot hammayim techilla qodem sheyyirchatz viqanneach bahem, deim yesh bahem nemalim lo yirchatz bahem. veken tzerikim lehizzaher poh irenu y" - sheyyesh bekol chatzar beer mayim chayyim, ak hem meluchim, veloqechim mayim mehem bishbil rechitzat yadayim o kelim, ubeellu hammayim matzuy tolaim sheqqorin bearbi "alaq", vehem neheragim birchitzat yadayim veshipshup veken bekelim. veod yesh bekelim chashasha gam bime hachol, shennidbaqim bahem tolaim ellu, veaach"k yitarebu im hammaakol shemmannichim bahem, velaken yizzaharu lesannen tamid hammayim techilla.

clarification.explanation: One should not walk in a place with many small creatures (ants), even without intending to kill them, since this is "an inevitable result that he would prefer not happen" (they will certainly be killed). In summer one must be careful about water in bathroom washing vessels into which ants have entered, and about brackish wells with worms in them — one should always check before use and filter the water. There is also a concern about this during the week: the worms stick to vessels and later mix into food placed in them.
takeaways: One avoids walking where there are ants; water is checked and filtered before use, to prevent unintentionally killing small creatures
